intro: I'm a Cybersecurity student in Karachi with hands-on exposure beyond the classroom — practicing vulnerability discovery and exploitation with tools like Burp Suite, Nmap, Wireshark, and John the Ripper, and competing in university CTF competitions covering cryptography and encryption/decryption challenges.
I'm looking to turn that foundation into an internship in SOC operations, penetration testing, or red teaming, where I can keep building practical skills alongside experienced security teams.
strengths: Hands-on with Burp Suite, Nmap, Wireshark, and John the Ripper
Vulnerability assessment and exploitation against practice targets (Metasploitable)
CTF competitor — cryptography and encryption/decryption challenges
Competitive programmer — Coders Cup (algorithms, debugging under time pressure)

projects.title: Client-Server Keylogging & Network Scanning System
projects.description: Built a Windows keylogger in C++ with Python socket-based server communication, auto-start via batch scripting, file transfer over sockets, Nmap-based IP discovery, and simulated RDP access control.
projects.outcome: Combined offensive security concepts (keylogging, network reconnaissance) with systems programming in a single client-server tool.

projects.title: Security Labs & CTF Practice
projects.description: Hands-on vulnerability discovery and exploitation using Burp Suite, Nmap, Wireshark, and John the Ripper against intentionally vulnerable targets like Metasploitable, plus university CTF competitions covering cryptography and encryption/decryption challenges using Kali Linux.
projects.outcome: Built practical, tool-based experience in vulnerability scanning, exploitation, and cryptographic challenges outside the classroom.
